quotes.text: Customize the card brands that Checkout displays.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: To block specific card brands, include the `brands_blocked` parameter when you create a Checkout Session.
The `discover_global_network` value encompasses all of the cards that are part of the Discover Global Network, including Discover, Diners, JCB, UnionPay, and Elo.

Checkout also filters cards in Apple and Google Pay wallets, customer’s [saved payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/save-during-payment.md), and [networks from co-badged cards](https://docs.stripe.com/co-badged-cards-compliance.md).

findings: The complete new capture contains only a title, purpose sentence and three variant links: Full page, Elements with Checkout Sessions, and Embedded form. It gives no brands_blocked schema, UI behavior, wallet filtering, API/version, or payment outcome contract. The Elements link is navigation to an unread variant, not evidence that old hosted/embedded behavior applies to it (new raw lines 5-15).

The fully read 2026-04-20 paired capture documents Checkout Session payment_method_options.card.restrictions.brands_blocked for hosted and embedded modes, with visa, mastercard, american_express and discover_global_network values. The last covers Discover, Diners, JCB, UnionPay and Elo. Blocked cards receive an error; filtering extends to Link saved cards, Apple/Google Pay wallets, saved payment methods and co-badged networks. These are dated hosted/embedded claims, not newly verified by the index (old raw lines 8-59, 61-113; source lines 11-34).

The old hosted example uses success_url, while the embedded example uses return_url and ui_mode=embedded_page. Those Session parameters and display errors concern Checkout configuration and card acceptance; a Session creation, return URL, or unblocked card does not prove successful payment (old raw lines 23-49, 76-103; source lines 22-34).

The source accurately summarizes the older hosted/embedded capture, carries its 2026-04-20 date, and links the Checkout concept. The new ui=full-page/ui=checkout-form parameters and the additional ui=elements link change navigation taxonomy, but do not prove the old payment-ui URLs or embedded_page parameter deprecated (old raw lines 8-10, 61-63, 83-100; new raw lines 9-15; source lines 1-43).
